item.title: Serious assault puts 'dampner' on Christmas in Ballaghaderreen - Scally
item.description: Gardaí are appealing for witnesses following a serious assault in Ballaghadereen. The incident occurred at around 1am yesterday morning on Barrack Street. Gardaí say a man in his 30s was brought to Beaumont Hospital, Dublin, where he remains in a critical condition. A Senior Investigating Officer has been appointed and an incident room has been established in Castlerea Garda Station. item.title: Man arrested in connection with serious assault in Ballaghaderreen
item.description: A man has been arrested in connection with a serious assault in Roscommon which left another man in a critical condition. The injured man in his 30s is being treated in Beaumont Hospital in Dublin following the incident on Barrack Street in Ballaghaderreen in the early hours of yesterday morning. This afternoon, Gardaí arrested a man in his 40s in connection with the incident. He's being questioned at a Garda station in the north-west, where he can be held for up to 24 hours. item.title: Sinn Féin calls for lessons after winter flu surge
item.description: Sinn Féin says lessons must be learned from this winter's flu surge. Health Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill is concerned about a second wave of the virus putting more pressure on hospitals next week. Sinn Féin's Health Spokesperson David Cullinane says resources are needed before flu strikes. Advertisement

item.title: Local Minister of State looks ahead to 2026
item.description: A recently-appointed Minister of State says he is looking forward to continuing his work in 2026. Frank Feighan was named as Minister of State at the Department of Public Expenditure with responsibility for public procurement, digitisation and E-Government in mid-November. The Sligo-Leitrim TD previously held the role of Minister of State at the Department of Health in 2020. item.title: Gardaí step up enforcement as Christmas period ends
item.description: Gardaí will be out in force across the region this weekend as the Christmas period comes to an end. The operation aims to curb speed related collisions and curb drink and drug driving and will continue until Monday. Gardaí, will target dangerous driving, reminding motorists that speeding endangers lives and increases the risk of fatal accidents. Advertisement Sergeant Stephen McDonagh from the Roscommon Roads Policing Unit says time will be allocated to enforce the campaign.

item.title: Status yellow snow and ice warning in place across Shannonside region
item.description: A status yellow snow and ice warning is in place across the entire Shannonside region this evening. It affects Longford, Leitrim and Roscommon from 6pm today until 11am tomorrow. Temperatures are set to fall as low as minus four degrees, with wintry showers, frost and icy patches expected. Advertisement Drivers are being urged to avoid unnecessary travel, with hazardous conditions and poor visibility forecast. item.title: Feasibility study underway for potential hotel in Boyle
item.description: A feasibility study is currently being carried out regarding a potential hotel being opened in Boyle. The North Roscommon Town has been without a hotel for around 15 years. It's been confirmed that the Irish Hot Air Ballooning Championships will return to Lough Key Forest Park next year. Advertisement Roscommon County Council Chief Executive Shane Tiernan says a new hotel would be a boost for tourism.

item.title: Gardaí attending scene of collision in Co. Longford
item.description: Gardaí are attending the scene of a collision in Co. Longford. The incident occurred this evening along the N4 near the Maria Edgeworth roundabout in Edgeworthstown. No injuries or fatalities have yet been confirmed, while the Longford Rd adjacent to Paul & Vincent has been closed. Gardaí have confirmed local diversions are in place and the road closure is set to be held for the night. More to follow. Advertisement

item.title: Man (30s) dies in Longford crash
item.description: A man has died in a crash in Longford. Two cars and a van collided on the Longford town side of the N4 after the Edgeworthstown roundabout at around 7pm. The driver of one of the cars, a man aged in his 30s, has been pronounced dead. Advertisement Another man, also aged in his 30s, has been taken to hospital with serious injuries, but they aren't life-threatening. No one else was injured.
